b24.why: 'First, the costume.' - hands behind back, quietly working out step one of the plan (not the eureka finger of the beat before); pull back opens the room he plots in
'He forged letterhead from the French government' - pen on official paper under a lamp; slow push onto the fake crest

b25.why: 'he gave himself a title' - open palm presenting himself like an official introducing his rank as he walks in; pan right follows his walk toward the brass 'Postes et Telegraphes' sign, and the label card spells the title out

b26.why: 'Why that ministry?' - hand-on-chin doubter voices the viewer's question; still camera lets the question hang
'the tower already carried radio equipment. It sounded real.' - aha finger, pan right to the lit tower, telegram pops as the radio link

b27.why: 'Then the stage. The Hotel de Crillon' - pull back reveals the grand facade; Lustig small and calm before it, sizing up his theatre

'one of the most expensive hotels in Paris' - he strolls in from the right, case in hand, toward the lit doors where a doorman bows; pan left follows his walk, mirrored so it does not echo the dealers' arrival in b33

b28.why: 'A palace, with doormen, and chandeliers.' - open palm presents the room like a host; push under the chandeliers, doorman frames right

b29.why: 'He understood something simple.' - teaching finger, flipped to face the room; hotel keys drop as the room becomes his tool

b30.why: 'Then the audience. He did not want rich men.' - hands behind back, choosing his marks; actor right of the window, quiet drift
'He wanted men who wanted to be richer.' - ambitious scrap dealer eyeing a falling coin among his iron; push into his hunger

b31.why: 'Each one invited by a polite, official letter' - dealer opening the sealed envelope, flattered; a gentle pull back as it slides up keeps the moment polite, saving the tight push for what the letter says in b32

b32.why: 'The letter said only this.' - tight push onto the letter in his hands, night street so the reading feels private

'Tell no one.' - the dealer tucks the sealed letter into his inner pocket with a glance over his shoulder: the secret obeyed, shown by the mark instead of a shush; locked camera under the dark tower keeps it hushed

b33.why: 'The dealers arrived thinking they had been picked.' - chest-out dealer strides to the hotel door, doorman bows; pan follows the walk

b34.why: 'the smallest detail could ruin him' - hands behind back, plotting, eyes on one small coin on the table; push narrows the frame down to the single tiny detail

'One wrong word, and six men could walk out.' - a suspicious chin-hand guest and a scrap dealer who puts one foot toward the door, hat to chest, then freezes. Locked camera holds the threat: nobody has left yet

x10.why: 'The papers, the title, the hotel' - explaining finger as each item pops on its word in turn; pan right walks the checklist
'the order he would speak in' - rehearsing his speech mouth-open, hand gesturing, flipped toward the window; pull back = alone, practising

x11.why: 'One slip' - Lustig hunched in the 'about to be caught' pose outside the hotel, a small jolt as if he has misstepped; pull widens and leaves him exposed in the empty street

'and call the police' - an imagined dealer, hands to cheeks as the truth lands, while a telegram rises beside him: the report he would send. Drift keeps it a threat, not an arrest (no police came for the first sale)

x12.why: 'The whole plan lived or died in one afternoon.' - suitcase in hand he walks toward the tower at sunset, the forged papers rise beside him; push in = no turning back
